StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single, and this power leaves Power.on_stack alone, so both sides add on re-application -- PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 has no StackType branch and Single means only 'Amount is hidden' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13). Correct, unlike the 15 units that override on_stack to a no-op citing the same StackType (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`).

AfterCardEnteredCombat.issue: DERIVED, not closed by analogy to smoggy (round 13, R5). RingingPower.cs differs: AfterApplied (:23-31) sweeps AllCards and afflicts EVERY unafflicted card OF ANY TYPE, where SmoggyPower filters to Skills; AfterCardEnteredCombat (:33-39) afflicts ONE arriving card and does not sweep. Same verdict split as smoggy: FALSE for a non-Power card mid-play (the old code parked it in the discard, so it was inside all_cards), TRUE for a Power card mid-play (HEAD put it in NO pile). Narrow, real, and dormant for the recorded reason -- Ringing is applied by an enemy on the enemy's turn. Now structurally fixed by the Play pile and pinned.  The text it replaced read: The owner filter is dropped, which is harmless in single-player, but the SITE is not: C# afflicts from AfterCardEnteredCombat (RingingPower.cs:34-40) and the sim's on_card_entered_combat (hooks.py:402-407) is fired only where the sim happens to call it. Recorded as a gap because the sim's __init__ walks `getattr(owner, 'all_cards', ())` (powers.py:1745) and PlayerCombatState.all_cards is `hand + draw + discard + exhaust` evaluated live (player.py:100-103) -- it does NOT include cards currently in the Play pile, i.e. a card mid-resolution. C# reads PlayerCombatState.AllCards, which is Hand, Draw, Discard, Exhaust AND Play (PlayerCombatState.cs:70-80). So a Ringing applied while a card is mid-play leaves that card unafflicted in the sim and afflicts it in the game. This is PROMPT.md bug class 7 (pile limbo) in its power form. DORMANT: Ringing is applied by an enemy on the enemy's turn, when no player card is mid-play. Named trigger: any player-side or mid-resolution Ringing application. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the player-side leg moved off the sim's Hook.BeforeTurnEnd slot (`on_player_turn_end`) onto `after_player_turn_end`, which combat.py:1796 dispatches AFTER `_process_turn_end_cards` and the hand flush -- the sim's port of Hook.AfterTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1307), the dispatcher for AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292). VERIFIED by reading combat.py:1765-1799 and this power's class in powers.py. WAS: the effect ran inside Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, so its order relative to the turn-end card effects, the flush and Stampede's turn-end auto-plays was hook registration order. The registration-order witness is doubly gone: StampedePower also moved, to `after_auto_post_play_phase_entered` (powers.py:1384), dispatched from a phase strictly before this slot.
